sub_answers.sub_question: Were there documented disputes or controversies related to hosting, bidding, or government involvement in the 2016 tournament?
What criticisms or official complaints were made regarding match officiating, eligibility, or competitive integrity during the 2016 event?
Were there reported logistical failures, cost overruns, or delays that drew public or media scrutiny during or after the tournament?
What limitations or shortcomings in the tournament's legacy delivery, sustainability, or impact evaluation were identified in post-event reports?
What changes in youth and women's football participation rates in Papua New Guinea and Oceania were recorded after the 2016 tournament?
What legacy projects, infrastructure uses, or development programs were established in Papua New Guinea following the 2016 event?
How did the tournament affect coaching, refereeing, and administrative capacity-building programs in the Oceania region?
What documented economic, tourism, or community development outcomes in Papua New Guinea are attributed to hosting the 2016 tournament?
What were the dates, host cities, and venues for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea?
Which national teams qualified for and participated in the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup?
Which team won the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup and what were the final match score and medalists?
What were the official attendance figures, television coverage, and reported economic figures for the 2016 tournament?
What stadiums, training facilities, and upgrades were used or constructed for the 2016 U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea?
What transport, accommodation, and accreditation systems were implemented for teams, officials, and fans during the tournament?
What roles did FIFA, the Papua New Guinea Football Association, and the local government play in operational planning and delivery?
What security, medical, and matchday operational procedures were documented for the 2016 tournament?

Were there any legal challenges, parliamentary inquiries, police investigations, ethics probes, or public protests tied to the tournament's host selection, bidding process, or government sponsorship and oversight for the 2016 event?

What formal protests, appeal filings to the tournament committee or sport federation, referee assessment reports, doping test disputes, or match-fixing allegations were lodged that questioned refereeing decisions, player eligibility, or the overall competitive integrity of matches in 2016?

Which specific operational problems—such as stadium construction or certification delays, public transport failures, security incidents, accreditation or accommodation shortages—or documented budget overruns and audit findings led to media coverage or official criticism during or after the 2016 tournament?

Which post-tournament evaluations, audit reports, academic studies, NGO assessments, or government reviews identified gaps in promised legacy programs, underuse of facilities, shortfalls in sustainability commitments, or weaknesses in how the event's economic and social impacts were measured after 2016?

How did youth enrollment numbers (by age group and gender) and registered female player counts in Papua New Guinea and other Oceania Football Confederation members change in the years 2016–2020, according to PNG Football Federation, OFC, FIFA or national sport surveys?

Which post-2016 legacy initiatives in Papua New Guinea—such as stadium upgrades, community pitches, school programs, or long-term facility maintenance plans—were launched, funded, or repurposed because of the 2016 tournament, and what are their documented timelines and managing organizations?

What evidence exists that the 2016 tournament led to expanded coaching, refereeing, or football administration education in Oceania—for example new coaching license courses, referee accreditation numbers, OFC workshops, or scholarships—and which organizations reported these capacity-building outcomes?

Which measurable economic, tourism, or local community impacts in Papua New Guinea (e.g., visitor numbers, hotel occupancy rates, local business revenue, employment linked to the event, or community social programs) have been attributed to hosting the 2016 tournament in government, tourism board, or independent post-event evaluations?

Provide the exact tournament dates for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Papua New Guinea, and list every host city along with the specific stadium/venue name used for matches (include which matches—opening, group stage, semifinals, final—were played at each venue).

List all national teams that qualified for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup (include the full 16-team roster), and for each team give its confederation and the qualification tournament or route by which it earned a spot.

Identify the tournament champion of the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup and provide the final match result (scoreline), the opposing finalist, and the teams that finished second and third (medalists), including goalscorers and whether the final was decided in regulation, extra time, or by penalties.

Report the official total and per-match attendance figures published for the 2016 tournament; list the primary television broadcasters or rights holders by country/region, any available broadcast viewership numbers or ratings, and any reported economic figures or impact assessments (ticket revenue, tournament budgets, government or LOC financial statements) related to staging the event in Papua New Guinea.

List the specific stadiums and training venues used for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Papua New Guinea (include official names, locations, seating capacities) and describe any new construction or renovation works completed for the tournament (scope of works, construction/upgrade dates, budgets, principal contractors and funders).

Describe the transport, accommodation and accreditation arrangements provided for participating teams, match officials and spectators during the 2016 tournament: identify shuttle or dedicated transport services (routes, schedules, vehicle types), host hotels and room allocations per delegation, fan transit plans, accreditation categories and the technology or systems used for issuing and managing accreditations and match tickets.

Detail the roles, responsibilities and agreements between FIFA, the Papua New Guinea Football Association (PNGFA) and Papua New Guinea national and provincial government bodies in delivering the 2016 event: cite formal memoranda of understanding, funding commitments, steering/organising committee structures, lines of operational responsibility, key deliverables assigned to each party and any reported delays or disputes.

Provide documented matchday operational protocols used at the 2016 tournament covering security and crowd management (police/steward numbers, crowd-control measures, perimeter security, evacuation plans), medical and emergency response arrangements (on-site medical staffing, ambulance coverage, trauma/triage plans, anti-doping and player-welfare procedures), and routine match operations (pitch maintenance schedules, ball/staffing procedures, referee liaison, contingency plans for weather or power failures).
What documented controversies, legal challenges, or allegations involving host-city selection, bid processes, or government sponsorship/influence were reported in connection with the 2016 tournament?

Which formal protests, referee assessment reports, player eligibility investigations, or federation rulings criticized officiating or competitive fairness at the 2016 event, and what specific incidents were cited?
Which media investigations, audit findings, or public records documented logistical breakdowns, budget overruns, contractor disputes, or schedule postponements linked to the 2016 tournament?

Which post-tournament audits, independent evaluations, or NGO reports identified gaps in planned legacy projects, failures in sustainability commitments, or weaknesses in measuring the 2016 event’s long-term economic and social impacts?

Which statistical changes were observed in girls' and young women's registered football players, school-level participation rates, and junior club memberships in Papua New Guinea and other Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) nations in the years immediately after the 2016 tournament (2016–2019)?

What named legacy initiatives, stadium or pitch renovations, community sports facilities, youth academies, or long-term grassroots development programs were launched, funded, or repurposed in Papua New Guinea as a direct result of hosting the 2016 tournament, and which agencies or donors supported them?

What evidence exists that the 2016 tournament led to expanded coaching, referee accreditation courses, technical officer training, or governance/administration workshops across OFC members — including numbers trained, new certification programs introduced, or partnerships formed between national associations and FIFA/OFC?

Which measurable economic indicators, tourism statistics (visitor numbers, hotel occupancy), local business revenues, or community social-development projects in Papua New Guinea have been explicitly linked in reports or evaluations to hosting the 2016 tournament, and what sources attribute those impacts?

Provide the exact tournament dates and a complete list of host locations for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup in Papua New Guinea, including each match venue name and the city or town where each stadium is located.

List every national team that qualified for and competed in the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup, organized by FIFA confederation (AFC, CAF, CONCACAF, CONMEBOL, OFC, UEFA) and indicating whether any teams entered as hosts or via intercontinental playoffs.

Identify the tournament winner of the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup and give the final match result (scoreline), the runner-up, the third- and fourth-placed teams, and the official podium/medal placements.

Report the official total and per-match attendance figures for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup, the broadcasters or networks that held TV rights (and any available viewership numbers), and any published economic figures or impact assessments (organizing costs, government spending, tourism revenue, or local economic impact) related to the event.

Which specific venues (stadiums and dedicated training grounds) were renovated, newly built, or repurposed for the 2016 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Papua New Guinea, and what were the scope, timelines, contractors, and budget figures for each upgrade or construction project?

How were teams, match officials, delegation support staff, and spectators accommodated and transported during the event—specifically which hotels were contracted, what shuttle/transport fleets and routes were used, what accreditation categories and credentialing processes were issued, and how were logistics for arrivals/departures managed?

How were responsibilities divided among FIFA headquarters, the Papua New Guinea Football Association (PNGFA), provincial/state authorities and the national government for planning, financing, staffing, and decision-making—what formal agreements, steering committees, or memorandum-of-understanding documents outline these roles?

What were the documented matchday operational plans for the tournament covering security arrangements (perimeter control, crowd management, emergency response), medical services (on-site EMS, stadium clinics, concussion and heat-stress protocols), and standard operating procedures for referees, venue operations, and contingency incidents?
